understanding: The task requires implementing a Telegram alert reporter for the OKO service that sends notifications only for VLM-described events (human/animal detections). The reporter must be in src/oko/live/reporters.py, implement EventReporter.report, use a specific alert format, read credentials from secrets file and environment/config, be disabled by default, and support injectable transport for testing. Additionally, service.py must default to configs/live-webcam.yaml and conditionally add TelegramReporter when OKO_TG_CHAT is set. All tests must pass.
summary: Implement TelegramReporter class in reporters.py that filters for VLM events and sends formatted alerts via Telegram API. Update service.py to use live-webcam.yaml as default config and conditionally register TelegramReporter based on OKO_TG_CHAT environment variable. Write tests verifying VLM-only filtering, correct API calls, and conditional activation.

decision_atoms.statement: TelegramReporter will filter events by checking for VLM description presence before sending any alert
decision_atoms.reason: Constraint requires alerts ONLY for events with VLM descriptions (human/animal detections), not for object-only events
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds a conditional check in report() method, slightly increasing complexity but ensuring compliance with the filtering requirement

decision_atoms.statement: TelegramReporter will accept an injectable transport parameter for HTTP requests
decision_atoms.reason: Constraint requires transport to be injectable for offline testing, enabling test doubles to verify API calls without network
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds constructor parameter and dependency injection pattern, increasing testability at cost of slightly more complex initialization

decision_atoms.statement: TelegramReporter will read bot token from ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json and chat_id from environment variable or config
decision_atoms.reason: Constraints specify exact sources: token from secrets file field 'telegramBotToken', chat_id from OKO_TG_CHAT env var or service configuration
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Couples reporter to file system and environment, but provides flexibility for different deployment scenarios

decision_atoms.statement: TelegramReporter will be disabled by default and only enabled when chat_id is provided
decision_atoms.reason: Constraint requires reporter to be OFF by default and enabled only when chat_id is configured
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires initialization logic to check for chat_id presence, preventing accidental alerts but adding startup validation

decision_atoms.statement: service.py will default config_path to 'configs/live-webcam.yaml' instead of example.yaml
decision_atoms.reason: Constraint requires service to work with webcam out-of-the-box using live-webcam.yaml as default
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Changes default behavior from example to production-ready config, which may surprise developers expecting example config but satisfies the out-of-box requirement

decision_atoms.statement: service.py will conditionally add TelegramReporter to reporters list when OKO_TG_CHAT environment variable is set
decision_atoms.reason: Constraint requires TelegramReporter to be added to active reporters list only when OKO_TG_CHAT is configured
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds environment variable check in service initialization, coupling service to environment but enabling dynamic reporter activation

assumptions: Event objects have a method or attribute to check for VLM description presence (e.g., has_vlm_description or vlm_description field)
EventReporter interface defines a report(event) method signature
The secrets file ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json exists and contains a 'telegramBotToken' field
The Telegram API endpoint for sending messages is https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage
The transport object has a post(url, json) method or similar interface
configs/live-webcam.yaml exists and is a valid configuration file
The service initialization code reads reporters from configuration or constructs them programmatically
pytest test suite exists and can be extended with new tests

risks.risk: Secrets file may not exist or have incorrect structure, causing runtime errors
risks.mitigation: Implement graceful error handling with clear error messages when secrets file is missing or malformed

risks.risk: Telegram API rate limits or network failures could cause alert delivery failures
risks.mitigation: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and log failures without crashing the service

risks.risk: VLM description format may vary, causing alert format to be inconsistent
risks.mitigation: Sanitize and truncate description if needed, document expected VLM description format

risks.risk: Changing default config from example.yaml to live-webcam.yaml may break existing workflows expecting example config
risks.mitigation: Document the change clearly in commit messages and consider adding a command-line override for config path

minimal_version: Implement TelegramReporter class with VLM filtering, injectable transport, secrets/env config reading, and default-disabled behavior. Update service.py default config path and conditional TelegramReporter registration. Write basic tests verifying VLM-only filtering and correct API call format.
advanced_version: Add retry logic with exponential backoff for Telegram API calls, implement message queuing for offline scenarios, add structured logging for alert delivery status, support multiple chat_ids, add configuration validation on startup, and implement comprehensive integration tests with mock Telegram server.
